# parity-fuzz --mode zutil baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode zutil --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (four seeds).
#
# Covers zsh/zutil: zstyle pattern precedence and lookup, zparseopts' option
# grammar, and zformat's field expansion.
#
# The mode already existed and ran clean, but was NOT gated in CI, so nothing
# stopped a regression in it. Gating is what makes that clean run mean
# something. `trap` and `redir` sat in exactly this state and each turned out
# to be hiding real bugs once their vocabulary was widened — a clean ungated
# mode is an untested mode, not a correct one.
#
# The vocabulary covered half of each builtin's option table and was widened
# against the C dispatch:
#
#   zstyle (c:Src/Modules/zutil.c:588-597) — table is `d s b a t T m q g`, plus
#   `L` (list as re-runnable syntax) and `e` (value is evaluated). Generated
#   were only `-a -d -m -s -t`; added `-b -T -g -L`.
#     `-T` is not `-t`: it returns TRUE when the style is not set at all, where
#     `-t` returns 2. `-b` writes yes/no into a variable AND sets $? from it.
#     `-g` retrieves style NAMES rather than a value.
#
#   zparseopts (c:Src/Modules/zutil.c bin_zparseopts) — flags are `D E F G K`
#   plus the `-a`/`-A` destinations. Generated were only `-D -E`; added
#   `-F -K -a -A`.
#     `-F` fails and diagnoses on an option outside the spec instead of leaving
#     it in argv. `-K` KEEPS the destination array's existing contents when the
#     option is absent instead of emptying it (so it only shows a difference
#     against a pre-seeded array — the generator seeds one). `-a`/`-A` collect
#     every match into one array/assoc rather than per-option arrays.
#
# TWO FLAGS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GENERATED — zshrs implements them CORRECTLY
# and the 5.9.2 oracle does not have them:
#
#   zstyle -q       oracle: `invalid option: -q`
#                   added upstream by c72b4a74ef ("52473: zstyle -q for testing
#                   existence of a zstyle setting")
#   zparseopts -G   oracle: `no default array defined: -G` — it does not know
#                   the flag and misreads it as an option spec
#                   added upstream by d051857e03 ("53260: zparseopts: add
#                   options -v (argv) and -G (GNU-style parsing)")
#
# Both post-date the oracle (Homebrew zsh-5.9.2-0-gddee3e7) while being present
# in the C reference fork (upstream master). Generating them would fail the gate
# for behaviour that is RIGHT. This is the same fork-ahead-of-oracle split as
# the `:S` history modifier and `typeset -n` namerefs, and it has a recognisable
# signature: zshrs accepts the feature, the oracle answers `invalid option` or
# misparses it. Check `git log -S` in the fork before treating that shape as a
# zshrs bug.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
